caveats: Requires restart-during-stop usage: one application thread calling start() while another thread's stop()/close() is still in progress (deployment model unconfirmed).
Requires the start thread's schedule+assign to land after stop began but before stop's read of timeoutListenerFuture; scheduling timing outside the tree decides whether this window is hit.
subclaims.reason: Thread A calls SshServer.stop (sshd-core/src/main/java/org/apache/sshd/server/SshServer.java:361, getAndSet(false)) or SshClient.stop (sshd-core/src/main/java/org/apache/sshd/client/SshClient.java:467), then close() runs removeSessionTimeout via getInnerCloseable. Thread B concurrently calls start(), which passes its guards because isStarted() is now false (SshServer.java:305) and isClosed() stays false until the inner close completes (sshd-common/src/main/java/org/apache/sshd/common/util/closeable/AbstractInnerCloseable.java:48, sshd-common/src/main/java/org/apache/sshd/common/util/closeable/AbstractCloseable.java:138-140), then schedules a new task into timeoutListenerFuture (sshd-core/src/main/java/org/apache/sshd/common/helpers/AbstractFactoryManager.java:479-480). Thread A's stopSessionTimeoutListener then reads that same field (AbstractFactoryManager.java:493) and cancels the newly scheduled task (AbstractFactoryManager.java:495), nulling the field and also removing the new generation's listener (AbstractFactoryManager.java:503-508), so the restarted manager runs with no session-timeout monitoring. The fields are plain non-volatile with no synchronized block or common lock between setup and stop, and the AtomicBoolean `started` only guards entry (both threads legitimately proceed), so no happens-before ordering rules the interleaving out; restart is anticipated usage per the comment at AbstractFactoryManager.java:501-502.
